note: Input layer, action queues: the helpers ActionQueue uses.

items.name: ActionData::ActionData
items.plate_base: ActionData::ActionData(int, float, int) (PS2 0x165188). Stores its first argument (the action id) at +0, the third at +4 and the float at +8.

items.name: ActionRef::ActionRef
items.plate_base: ActionRef::ActionRef(ActionData *): the 4-byte handle ActionQueue::GetAction returns - it stores the pointer. Its body (store one dword, return this) is generic enough that other 4-byte constructors may be folded onto it.

items.name: ActionQueueRing::Push
items.plate_exact: INVENTED NAME, not canonical: the ring buffer inside ActionQueue has no PS2 symbol (the PS2 build inlines it). Appends an ActionData at the tail (wrapping at capacity); when the ring is full the oldest action is dropped (head advances, count stays at capacity). Called by ActionQueue::ReceiveAction on this+4.

items.name: ActionQueueRing::ActionQueueRing
items.plate_exact: INVENTED NAME, not canonical: the ring buffer inside ActionQueue has no PS2 symbol (the PS2 build inlines it). Constructs the 200 ActionData slots (0, 0, 0) and sets count 0, tail -1, head 0, capacity 200. Called by ActionQueue's constructor on this+4.
